# Code of Conduct

## The standard

Be decent to the people you are working with. Concretely, in issues, pull requests, reviews
and any other space belonging to this project:

- Critique the work, not the person. "This breaks on empty input" is useful; "this is
  sloppy" is not.
- Assume the other person is competent and acting in good faith until you have real
  evidence otherwise. Most disagreements are missing context, not bad intent.
- Accept that maintainer time is finite. A change may be declined because it does not fit
  the project, not because it is bad.
- Harassment, personal attacks, discriminatory language, and deliberate disruption are not
  welcome here, in any form and regardless of who they come from.

## Scope

This applies in all project spaces, and when you are representing the project elsewhere.

## Enforcement

Report anything that concerns you through
[GitHub's private reporting form](https://github.com/arnoldwender) or, if the issue is with
project content rather than a person, by opening an issue.

Reports are read by the maintainer. Depending on what happened, the response may be a
correction, the removal of a comment, or a block. Serious or repeated behaviour ends
participation in the project.

This document is deliberately short. It is not a legal instrument — it is a statement of
what is expected, so that nobody has to guess.
